The National Career Service (NCS) portal is a vital digital platform by the Indian government, designed to transform the employment landscape. This guide provides a concise overview of the NCS portal, its core functions, and how it serves jobseekers, employers, counselors, and other stakeholders.

**What is the NCS Portal?**

The NCS portal, accessible at [www.ncs.gov.in](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncs.gov.in%2F), is a government initiative to connect jobseekers with employment opportunities. It provides a range of services, including job matching, career guidance, and skill development information.

**Key Functions for Different Users**

The portal offers specific functionalities for various users:

* **Jobseekers** can register, search for jobs, access career resources, and manage their profiles.
* **Employers** can post job vacancies, search for candidates, and manage the recruitment process.
* **Career Centers** can organize job fairs, provide counseling, and manage reports.
* **Counsellors** can schedule sessions, manage appointments, and offer guidance.
* **Skill Providers** can add courses, manage training centers, and connect with trainees.
* **Local Service Providers** can register, access job postings, and provide feedback.

**How to Register and Login**

To register on the NCS portal:

1. Click “New User? Sign Up” on the Home page.
2. Select your user type (Jobseeker, Employer, etc.).
3. Fill in the required details and create a password.
4. Verify your mobile number and email ID using OTP.
5. Click “Submit” to complete registration.

To login:

1. Enter your User Name.
2. Enter your Password.
3. Click “Sign In.”

**Key Features of the NCS Portal**

The NCS portal offers several key features:

* **User-Friendly Interface:** Easy navigation for all user types.
* **Job Search:** Robust search functionality with filters for location, sector, and salary.
* **Profile Management:** Tools to create and update personal and professional profiles.
* **Career Resources:** Access to counseling, skill development, and training information.
* **Job Fairs and Events:** Information on upcoming job fairs and events.
* **Direct Benefit Transfer:** Monetary rewards are directly transferred to trainees’ accounts.
* **Reporting and Analytics:** Access to detailed reports and analytics.

**Financial Assistance and Support**

The NCS portal supports various government initiatives, including the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), which provides monetary awards for skill certification.

**The NCS Portal in the Indian Context**

The NCS portal is a critical component of India’s Skill India Mission. It aims to reduce unemployment by connecting skilled individuals with suitable job opportunities, fostering a more stable and productive workforce.

**Conclusion**

The National Career Service (NCS) portal is a valuable resource for individuals and organizations in India’s employment ecosystem. By providing a digital platform for job search, recruitment, and skill development, the portal contributes to the nation’s economic growth and social progress.

# National Career Service Portal 2026: How to Register and Find Government Jobs

by [NILESH KUMAR](https://rupayasalah.in/author/nileshkumar90313gmail-com/ "View all posts by NILESH KUMAR")

## National Career Service Portal 2026: How to Register and Find Government Jobs

### Key Takeaways

* National Career Service Portal 2026 is India’s largest government job matching platform with over 1 crore registered job seekers.
* The NCS portal connects job seekers with government vacancies, private employers, apprenticeships, and career counselling — all in one place.
* Registration on ncs.gov.in is completely free for all Indian job seekers — no fees at any stage.
* Job seekers can access Rozgar Melas, skill development programs, and career guidance through the same portal.
* The portal is managed by the Ministry of Labour and Employment — making it the most authentic source for central and state government job notifications.

### Introduction

Every day thousands of young Indians search for government jobs online — visiting dozens of websites, missing important deadlines, and wasting hours on unreliable third-party portals. There is a better way — and it is completely free. **National Career Service Portal 2026** — commonly known as the **NCS Portal** — is the Government of India’s official one-stop digital platform for employment services, government job listings, private sector vacancies, apprenticeship opportunities, skill development programs, and career counselling. Managed by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, the NCS portal is the digital replacement for India’s traditional employment exchanges — bringing every employment service online in a single, transparent, and accessible platform. In 2026 with over 1 crore registered job seekers and thousands of active employers — the NCS portal is the most powerful free tool any job seeker in India has access to. This complete guide walks you through everything — what the portal offers, who should register, and the exact step-by-step process to create your profile, upload your resume, and start finding the right job today.

### What Is National Career Service Portal 2026?

**National Career Service Portal 2026** — available at **ncs.gov.in** — is a centrally managed digital employment platform launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India** on **20 July 2015** as part of the **National Career Service (NCS) Project**. It was designed to modernize and digitize India’s traditional employment exchange system — which had operated manually for decades with limited reach and effectiveness.

The NCS portal operates as a **multi-stakeholder ecosystem** — connecting four groups through a single platform:

* **Job Seekers** — Individuals looking for employment in government or private sector
* **Employers** — Government departments, PSUs, private companies, and SMEs posting vacancies
* **Skill Providers** — Training institutions, ITIs, polytechnics, and skill development centers
* **Career Counsellors** — Registered professionals providing career guidance and placement assistance

In 2026 the NCS portal covers:

* Over **1 crore registered job seekers** across all states and union territories
* More than **30 lakh registered employers** from government and private sectors
* Over **1.5 lakh active job vacancies** at any given time
* **20,000+ skill development course** listings from ITIs, polytechnics, and private training centers
* **Apprenticeship opportunities** from NAPS-registered establishments across India
* **Rozgar Mela job fair** registrations and schedules from all states

The portal is available in **Hindi and English** and has a dedicated **mobile application** for Android and iOS — making it accessible to job seekers across rural and urban India regardless of their device or location.

### Key Services Available on NCS Portal 2026

The NCS portal is far more than just a job listing website — it is a complete career development ecosystem offering eight distinct service categories:

#### Service 1 — Job Search and Application

The core function of the NCS portal — job seekers can search for vacancies across government departments, PSUs, private companies, and NGOs using filters for location, qualification, salary range, sector, and job type. Registered job seekers can apply for vacancies directly through the portal — and receive application status updates in real time.

#### Service 2 — Resume Building and Profile Management

Job seekers create a detailed digital profile on the NCS portal — including educational qualifications, work experience, skills, language proficiency, and career preferences. The portal has a built-in **resume builder tool** that generates a professional resume from the profile data — downloadable as a PDF and shareable with employers through the portal.

#### Service 3 — Career Counselling

The NCS portal connects job seekers with registered **Career Counsellors** — both online and at physical **National Career Service Centres (NCSCs)** — for guidance on career path selection, higher education options, skill gap analysis, interview preparation, and resume review. This service is especially valuable for students and fresh graduates making their first major career decision.

#### Service 4 — Rozgar Mela — Job Fairs

State governments and district employment offices organize **Rozgar Melas** — government-organized job fairs — where employers and job seekers meet directly for on-the-spot interviews and placements. All Rozgar Mela schedules, locations, and registration details are listed on the NCS portal — allowing job seekers to register in advance and appear prepared.

#### Service 5 — Apprenticeship Registration

The NCS portal integrates with the **National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)** — allowing job seekers to search for apprenticeship opportunities across 4,000+ registered establishments nationwide and register directly for apprenticeship training with government stipend support.

#### Service 6 — Skill Development Course Listings

Job seekers can browse and enroll in skill development courses from **ITIs, polytechnics, PMKVY centers, and private training partners** listed on the portal. Courses are searchable by location, duration, sector, and qualification level — making it easy to find relevant upskilling options near home.

#### Service 7 — Disability Employment Services

The NCS portal has a dedicated section for **Differently-Abled job seekers** — with special employer listings, accessible job search filters, and priority career counselling services. Employers posting vacancies for PwD-reserved positions are listed separately — improving visibility and matching for disabled job seekers.

#### Service 8 — Self-Employment and Entrepreneurship Guidance

Job seekers interested in self-employment can access information on government schemes — PMEGP, MUDRA, Stand Up India, Startup India — and connect with District Industries Centres and incubators through the NCS portal’s self-employment guidance module.

### NCS Portal 2026 — Who Should Register

#### Registration Is Beneficial For

| Profile | How NCS Portal Helps |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh graduates — BA BSc BCom | Access entry-level government and private job listings filtered by qualification |
| Engineering and technical graduates | Find PSU, government technical, and private sector technical vacancies |
| ITI and diploma holders | Find apprenticeship openings and skill-matched job listings |
| Experienced professionals | Upload detailed work history and apply for senior vacancies |
| School pass-outs — Class 10 and 12 | Find entry-level government jobs and vocational training courses |
| Women returning to workforce | Access part-time, remote, and returnship-friendly job listings |
| Differently-abled job seekers | Access PwD-reserved vacancies and specialized counselling |
| Ex-Agniveer veterans | Access CAPF and government department priority listings |
| Ex-servicemen | Find defence quota government vacancies and civilian transition jobs |
| Self-employment seekers | Connect with scheme information and entrepreneurship guidance |

### NCS Portal 2026 — Features and Benefits

The NCS portal delivers a unique combination of benefits that no private job portal can replicate — because it is government-operated, free, and directly connected to actual government hiring pipelines:

1. **Direct Government Vacancy Access** — Central and state government departments, PSUs, railways, defence civilian posts, and educational institutions post vacancies directly on NCS — giving registered job seekers first-hand access to authentic government job openings without intermediaries.
2. **Smart Job Matching** — The NCS portal uses a smart matching algorithm that automatically suggests relevant vacancies based on a job seeker’s educational qualifications, skills, location, and career preferences — saving hours of manual search time.
3. **Free Resume Builder** — The portal’s built-in resume tool creates a professionally formatted resume from your profile data — helping job seekers who lack resume writing skills present themselves effectively to employers.
4. **Real-Time Application Tracking** — Job seekers can track the status of every application submitted through the portal — knowing exactly whether their application has been viewed, shortlisted, or rejected by each employer.
5. **Rozgar Mela Pre-Registration** — Registering for Rozgar Melas through the NCS portal gives job seekers a confirmed slot with specific employers — eliminating the need to stand in long walk-in queues at physical job fairs.

7. **Pan-India Reach** — The NCS portal lists vacancies and opportunities from all 36 states and union territories — allowing job seekers to search nationwide or filter specifically to their home state and district.
8. **Mobile App Convenience** — The NCS mobile app allows complete job searching, application submission, Rozgar Mela registration, and profile management from any smartphone — making it accessible to job seekers in rural areas with limited internet access.

### Eligibility Criteria for NCS Portal Registration

| Category | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| Nationality | Indian citizen only |
| Age | Minimum 14 years — no upper age limit |
| Qualification | No minimum qualification required — any education level can register |
| Employment Status | Employed, unemployed, student, or self-employed — all can register |
| Location | Resident of any state or union territory in India |
| Registration Fee | Completely free — no fee at any stage |
| Documents Required | Aadhaar card and mobile number — basic registration only |
| Multiple Registrations | Only one profile per individual — duplicate profiles are rejected |

#### Documents Required for Complete Profile

* Aadhaar card — for identity verification and OTP-based login
* PAN card — optional but recommended for complete profile
* Educational certificates — Class 10, 12, graduation, postgraduate, and technical qualifications
* Work experience documents — appointment letters and experience certificates if applicable
* Skill or vocational training certificates — ITI, PMKVY, NAPS, or any skill certification
* Caste certificate — SC, ST, or OBC — for community-specific job filters
* PwD certificate — for differently-abled job seeker benefits
* Bank account details — for schemes linked through the portal
* Recent passport-size photograph
* Resume in PDF format — for direct upload alongside portal-generated resume

### How to Register and Use NCS Portal — Step-by-Step Process

Registering and setting up a complete job-ready profile on the NCS portal takes less than 30 minutes. Follow these eight steps without skipping any:

1. **Visit the official NCS portal** — Open your browser and go to **ncs.gov.in** — the only official Government of India employment portal. 2. **Click on “New User — Register Here” and select job seeker** — On the homepage find the registration section and click “New User.” Select “Job Seeker” as your user type — not employer or skill provider. Enter your full name exactly as on Aadhaar, date of birth, gender, mobile number, and email ID. Create a strong password and verify your mobile number with the OTP sent by the portal.
3. **Complete your basic profile with personal details** — After successful registration log in with your mobile number and password. Fill in your complete personal details — father’s name, mother’s name, date of birth, Aadhaar number, permanent address, current address, state, district, and pin code. Complete every field — incomplete profiles receive fewer job match suggestions from the algorithm.
4. **Add your complete educational qualifications** — Enter every educational qualification you hold — Class 10, Class 12, ITI, diploma, graduation, postgraduate, and any technical or professional certification. Include the institution name, board or university, year of passing, and percentage or grade obtained. The portal uses this data to match you with qualification-appropriate vacancies.
5. **Add work experience and skills** — If you have prior work experience add each job with employer name, designation, period of employment, and key responsibilities. Add all technical and soft skills you possess — computer skills, language proficiency, subject expertise, and vocational skills. The more complete your skills section the more relevant your job matches will be.

7. **Set your job preferences** — In the job preferences section specify your preferred job location — state and district, preferred sector — government, private, PSU, NGO — preferred job type — full-time, part-time, remote — expected salary range, and willingness to relocate. These preferences directly influence which vacancies appear in your daily job match suggestions.

### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Q1: What is the National Career Service Portal and who manages it in 2026?** The **National Career Service Portal 2026** — available at **ncs.gov.in** — is India’s official government employment platform managed by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India** under the NCS Project. It serves as the digital replacement for India’s traditional manual employment exchange system — connecting job seekers, employers, skill providers, and career counsellors through a single free online platform. In 2026 the portal has over 1 crore registered job seekers and 30 lakh registered employers making it the largest government-managed employment marketplace in India. It lists central and state government vacancies, PSU jobs, private sector jobs, apprenticeship opportunities, and skill development courses — all accessible for free through one registration.

**Q2: Is registration on the NCS portal free and how long does it take?** Yes — **NCS portal registration is completely free** at every stage — there is no registration fee, no profile creation charge, no job application fee, and no premium subscription required. The entire service is funded by the Government of India and provided free to all Indian job seekers regardless of their educational qualification, employment status, or state of residence. Basic registration — creating your account with name, mobile number, and basic details — takes approximately **5 to 10 minutes**. Completing a full profile — adding all educational qualifications, work experience, skills, resume, photo, and job preferences — typically takes **20 to 30 minutes** total. A complete profile is strongly recommended as it significantly increases employer visibility and job match accuracy.

**Q3: Can I find government jobs directly on the NCS portal in 2026?** Yes — the **NCS portal is one of the most direct sources for government job listings in India**. Central government departments, state government departments, PSUs, municipal corporations, defence civilian establishments, and educational institutions post vacancies directly on the NCS portal. Additionally the portal lists all **Rozgar Mela job fair** schedules organized by state employment departments — where government and PSU employers conduct direct on-the-spot recruitment drives. For central government technical and group posts — NCS portal notifications often appear before or simultaneously with postings on official department websites.

**Q4: How do I apply for jobs through the NCS portal in 2026?** After completing your NCS profile registration on **ncs.gov.in**, use the job search feature to find relevant vacancies using filters for location, qualification, salary range, and sector. When you find a suitable vacancy click the **“Apply”** button on the job listing page. Your registered profile — including your educational qualifications, experience, skills, resume, and photograph — is automatically shared with the employer through the portal. You receive an application confirmation on your registered email and mobile number. You can track the status of all submitted applications from your profile dashboard — seeing whether each application is under review, shortlisted, or rejected. For Rozgar Mela applications you register your slot through the “Job Fairs” section and receive a confirmation with reporting time and venue details.

**Q5: What is a National Career Service Centre and how is it different from the NCS portal?** A **National Career Service Centre (NCSC)** is a physical government-operated career guidance and employment facilitation office — located across India in major cities, district headquarters, and university campuses. NCSCs provide in-person services that complement the online NCS portal — including face-to-face career counselling sessions, resume review, mock interview practice, employer connect events, and direct job placement assistance. There are over **900 NCSCs** operational across India in 2026. The **NCS portal at ncs.gov.in** is the digital platform that works 24/7 for online job search, registration, and applications. Both the physical NCSCs and the online portal are part of the same **National Career Service ecosystem** managed by the Ministry of Labour — job seekers can use both simultaneously for maximum benefit.

### Conclusion

**National Career Service Portal 2026** is the most powerful, most authentic, and most accessible free employment tool available to every job seeker in India today — and the vast majority of eligible candidates have never used it to its full potential. With over 1 crore job seekers, 30 lakh employers, direct government vacancy listings, Rozgar Mela access, apprenticeship opportunities, skill course listings, and free career counselling — ncs.gov.in gives you everything you need to find the right job, build the right skills, and access the right opportunities without spending a single rupee. # National Career Service — the government's free job portal

[![National Career Service — the government's free job portal — RTI Wiki](https://righttoinformation.wiki/_media/social/auto/national-career-service.png?w=1200&tok=a575fb "National Career Service — the government's free job portal — RTI Wiki")](https://righttoinformation.wiki/_media/social/auto/national-career-service.png "social:auto:national-career-service.png")

**Quick Reply:** NCS at **ncs.gov.in** is the Ministry of Labour and Employment's free job portal, run by the Directorate General of Employment — job-seeker and employer registration, lakhs of live vacancies, counselling and skill-course links. The toll-free helpline is **1514**. NCS never charges a fee; anyone demanding one in its name is a scam.

## What the portal does

* **Job-seeker registration** — Aadhaar-linked signup, profile with education, skills, experience and preferred locations; matched vacancies surface on your dashboard.
* **Vacancies** — government and private postings indexed from across the country; the portal's own counters show lakhs of live vacancies at any time.
* **Career services** — career counselling, aptitude and skill assessment, and links to skill courses; Model Career Centres run in-person versions of the same services.
* **Job fairs** — rojgar mela listings by city and date, with direct registration.
* **International placement** — an overseas-jobs channel tied to the e-Migrate framework for legal overseas employment.
* **Employer side** — employers register with verification, post vacancies and shortlist; the portal publishes a **blacklisted-entities list** of employers caught misusing it.
* **Anti-fraud stand** — the portal's standing warning: **NCS never charges any fee** to job seekers at any stage.

## Registration, step by step

1. Go to [ncs.gov.in](https://www.ncs.gov.in "https://www.ncs.gov.in") and choose **Job Seeker** registration.
2. Verify with Aadhaar OTP; your name and date of birth fill automatically.
3. Complete the profile — education, skills, experience, languages, location preference — and upload a resume.
4. Set job alerts (SMS/email) by role and city.
5. Apply from the listing; track applications and interview calls on the dashboard.
6. Also register on your state employment exchange portal where one exists — the two systems serve different vacancy streams.

## The helpline and support

* **1514** — the Government of India toll-free NCS helpline, published on the portal's contact page.
* Email support: [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection).
* For scheme-level grievances, the **Directorate General of Employment** (Ministry of Labour & Employment) is the nodal body.

## Fraud patterns to know

* Fake “NCS registration fees” or “exam fees” — the portal is free; genuine employers on it cannot charge you to apply.
* Telegram and WhatsApp “NCS recruiters” offering jobs for a payment — verify the employer on the portal; use the blacklist check.
* Offers that bypass the portal entirely while using its name — treat as fraud and report on 1514.

## Career centres and exchanges — the offline layer

* **Model Career Centres** are the ministry's physical front-end for NCS — counselling, assessment and placement support in person; ask at the district employment office whether one runs near you.
* **State employment exchanges** still register candidates separately; their notification-of-vacancy channel is a different stream from NCS listings, so a serious job seeker uses both.
* **Job fairs** listed on the portal are real hiring events — registration on NCS is usually the entry pass; carry printed resumes.
* **Vocational guidance** for students choosing a stream is also a listed service — not only for the unemployed.

## The RTI angle

The Ministry of Labour and Employment and the DGE are public authorities with CPIOs. NCS itself is a mission-mode project of the ministry — it is not a creation of the four labour codes now in force (since 21 November 2025); the old Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act, 1959 remains a separate, unrepealed statute. Questions NCS users legitimately put through RTI:

```
1. The number of job-seeker registrations and vacancies listed on the NCS portal for [district/state] as on [date]. 2. The number of grievances received on NCS helpline 1514 in the last 12 months and their disposal rate. 3. The criteria and number of employers blacklisted from the portal to date, with the orders. 4. The number of Model Career Centres functional in [state] and the services each is mandated to provide. 5. The funds allocated and spent on the NCS project in the last financial year.
```

Address the CPIO, Directorate General of Employment, Ministry of Labour and Employment — the [AI RTI Drafter](https://righttoinformation.wiki/tools/ai-rti-draft-app.html "https://righttoinformation.wiki/tools/ai-rti-draft-app.html") fills the block.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is NCS only for government jobs?

No — private vacancies form the bulk of listings; government posts appear too.

### Does registration guarantee a job?

No portal can. NCS matches and connects; the interview and offer remain with the employer.

### Is there an age limit?

Job-seeker registration is open to citizens of working age; specific vacancies carry their own limits.

### Do I need to renew?

Keep the profile current — stale profiles sink in matching. Update after any course or job change.

### Is NCS the same as the employment exchange?

No — NCS is the national online portal; state employment exchanges run their own registration and notifications. Registering on both widens your vacancy stream.

### Can employers on NCS be fake?

The portal verifies employers and publishes a blacklist, but verify any offer yourself: no genuine employer on NCS charges a fee to applicants, and offers routed off-platform for “processing payments” are fraud — report them on 1514.

## National Career Service(NCS)

The Ministry is implementing the National Career Service (NCS) Project as a Mission Mode Project for transformation of the National Employment Service to provide a variety of employment related services like career counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill development courses, apprenticeship, internships etc. The NCS Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) was dedicated to the Nation by Hon'ble Prime Minister of India on 20.07.2015. The NCS Portal is supported by a dedicated helpline (multi-lingual) available from Tuesday to Sunday (8:00 A.M. to 8 P.M.) on 1514 for assisting users.

The National Career Services (NCS) initiative aims to address the gaps in the employment market by strategic interventions and partnership with leading institutions and organizations, improving decent employment, enhancing quality of workforce, enhancing female labour force participation, entrepreneurial endeavors, informal to formal transition, engaging with rural workforce for higher productivity, re-employment opportunities etc.

NCS is a one-stop solution that provides a wide array of employment and career related services to the citizens of India. It works towards bridging the gap between candidates and employers; candidates seeking training and career guidance and agencies providing training and career counseling.

The main objectives of NCS project are as follows:

* Enhancing career and employment opportunities
* Counselling and guidance for career development
* Enhancing quality of workforce
* Focusing on inclusive growth initiatives

1. ### International Vacancies

   NCS portal has provisioned to collect international job preference based on occupation and regional preference. The international vacancies are posted by the NCS registered recruitment agencies on the NCS portal. The registered jobseekers having matching skills are recommended to apply for the posts if they are interested.
2. ### Employability Trainings

   In partnership with the pioneers in the industry, NCS organizes various training program to augment the employability skills, cognitive as well as non-cognitive, of the jobseekers. Details of the employability training available on NCS portal for providing soft skill training and digital skills training are given below:

   1. Career Skills Training by TCS iON

      National Career Service (NCS) partnered with TCS iON, a strategic unit of Tata Consultancy Services Ltd. to offer its registered jobseekers a free, self-paced Online Training Program on “Career Skills”, which will equip the learners with an array of soft skills. The course is available in Hindi and English and covers modules like corporate etiquette, effective e-mail writing, preparing impactful presentations, Corporate Telephone Etiquette etc.
   2. “DigiSaksham” Job skills Training by Microsoft

      National Career Service partnered with Microsoft India and launched Digisaksham, a joint digital skills initiative for employability through digital skills. The project is focused on empowering the youth from rural & semi-urban areas to acquire digital skills, with a focus on rural and socially disadvantaged youth for better career opportunities. The free-of-cost online trainings are conducted in two modes viz. self-paced training and Virtual Instructor Led Training (VILT) on various courses of Microsoft such as Excel, Azure, Security Fundamentals etc. for enhancing the employability of the NCS registered candidates.
3. ### Career Counsellors

   NCS Portal provides online career counselling and vocational guidance services to its registered users. This service aims to equip the jobseeker with necessary information that is required to make right career choices based on his/her qualification, skill set and interest. The NCS Portal provides an opportunity to browse through the list of the approved counsellors and book an appointment with them. Counselling services would be made available on face-to-face basis or via online platforms. The main aim of career counselling is to assist the job seekers in choosing a field that is in tune with their skills and their career expectations. The NCS Project also envisages offering vocational guidance services through empanelled Vocational Guidance (VG) Experts, having requisite experience and expertise.

   Apart from the online counselling services, NCS Portal also provides on ground counselling services through its country wide network of Model Career Centers. Ministry of Labour and Employment has deployed trained Young Professionals and Counsellors at its various Model Career Centers under National Career Service Scheme who offer specialized Individual and Group Career Counselling. The policy for onboarding of Career counsellors may be seen at (www.ncs.gov.in).
4. ### Career Information Content

   NCS provides detailed career information across 52 sectors, on various job roles under each sector for use by Job aspirants. Career information under each sector has been made available in both video and text form on the Portal. For each sector, the videos focus on broad career streams and disciplines within a sector while the text information shares in-depth information about various job roles within that sector. Over 3600 Job roles that have been covered in total on NCS under various sectors are based on the National Classification of Occupation-2015, which is a compendium for occupational information available in the Indian Economy. NCO codes facilitate in making information in the Employment market more transparent and objective.
5. ### Job-fairs organized by Career Centres

   Job fairs are organized at Model Career Centres (MCCs) for facilitating the jobseekers to meet with the employers and thereafter leading to their placement. In turn, the employers who are searching for the right skills could find suitable candidates from the job fairs. In MCCs the job-fairs are being regularly organized online or on-campus job[1]fairs. For organizing on-line job-fairs provision has been provided in the NCS portal. The MCCs/employment Exchanges create the job-fair event in NCS portal the employers/placement organizations post their vacancies. The eligible candidates are notified about the vacancies through SMS/email. Additional efforts are also being taken by the MCCs/Employment Exchanges to mobilize the employers/placement organizations and jobseekers to participate in the job-fairs. While conducting the on[1]campus job-fairs, the career centres also create the event in the NCS portal.
6. ### Interlinkages of NCS portal

   The Directorate General of Employment, Ministry of Labour & Employment provides the fund to support the State/UT Governments for providing basic IT infrastructure, minor re-furbishing of the 997 employment exchanges and for organizing job fairs at the district level to enhance the placement of the jobseekers.

   For States having ICT based integrated systems for the employment exchanges, web services have been created for inter-linking state databases with the NCS Portal. NCS Portal has also been integrated with other Ministries/ departments like e-Shram MSDE, MHRD, AICTE, etc. Online integration with EPFO, ESIC and Shram Suvidha Portal have also been done to link the willing employers and enabling them to shortlist right candidates through a countrywide database of workforce on NCS portal.

   NCS has constantly been evolving significantly to enhance its reach through introduction of new services and features from time to time. Some of these features include integrations with DigiLocker to enable candidates to upload their documents/certificates and make them available to the employers to accelerate the hiring process and integration with HireMee for creation of short video profiles by the jobseekers as video Curriculum Vitae (CV).
7. ### Young Professional Scheme

   Ministry of Labour and Employment, under the Mission Mode Project is implementing the National Career Service (NCS) Project for revamping public employment related service. For the smooth transformation, as per the approved proposal of NCS project, Model Career Centres (MCCs) have been set up to provide standardized employment services across the nation. In order to make these MCCs effectively functional, a ‘Young Professional Scheme’ was launched by Directorate General for Employment (DGE) wherein one YP has been deployed at each MCC, for a span of 3 years, to facilitate the activities of the NCS Project. The ‘Young Professional Scheme’ has been aimed to utilize the knowledge, energy and fresh way of thinking of these young social leaders to help in the better transformation of the emerging landscape of employment service and career counselling in India. YP scheme was launched in 2015 and so far, 199 YPs have been recruited in 6 batches.

   The YPs are recruited on time-based contract, as the Young Professional has to be engaged for a fixed period not exceeding 5 years for providing high quality services on specific projects as per the requirement. However, their continuation in their respective position beyond the second and subsequent years, would be contingent on a satisfactory performance review based on clearly defined Key Performance indicators. At present the Young Professionals are paid a consolidated amount of Rs.50,000/- as monthly remuneration plus Rs.1,500/- as conveyance allowance. An annual increment of Rs.5000/- is also granted to the Young Professionals based on their performance review.
